Assistant: Of course!  Here's a recipe for a traditional Latvian dish, fillet of rudd.

Frikadeļu zupa

Serves 4

2 kg fillet of rudd (white fish)

2 tbsp olive oil

1 onion, finely chopped

2 garlic cloves, crushed

2 shallots, finely chopped

750 g potatoes, peeled, cut into
small cubes

8 carrots, peeled, cut into small
pieces

salt and pepper

5 tbsp flour

350 ml white wine

2 tbsp cold-pressed rapeseed oil

2 tbsp sour cream

Method

Place the fillet of rudd in a roasting pan and pour over cold water.  Cover with salt and
pepper.

Heat the oven to 200ºC/180ºC fan/gas mark 6.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until cooked through to the internal temperature of
the thickest part for medium -lrb- if you've an instant thermometer -rrb-
that will be about 4°C/36°F.  Leave to rest in the roasting pan for 5 minutes
before carving and serving.

For the mash, cut the potatoes into very small cubes and cover with cold
water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, stirring
frequently, until cooked.
Drain in a sieve under cold running water.

In a pan, heat the rapeseed oil.  Add the onion and garlic and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add the shallots and cook for a few minutes longer.

Add the flour and stir for a second.  Add the white wine and stir quickly, scraping
the bottom of the pan to remove the bits of flour that have stuck.  Slowly pour in the
potatoes and carrots, mixing together and stirring frequently.
Boil for about 5 minutes.  Season with salt and pepper and add the sour cream.
Turn down the heat and simmer until soft and well cooked, about 10 minutes.

To make the crumble, mix the flour with the salt and pepper and chop into bits.
Roll the mixture into balls about the size of a cherry.

Heat the rapeseed oil in a frying pan and fry the crumble balls on both
sides on a low heat.
Remove them with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Put the pan back on the heat and fry the onions until they are soft.
Stir in the egg yolks, sour cream and flour and cook over low heat whilst stirring
until it forms a thick, smooth sauce.

Season with salt and pepper and stir in the fricade and sour cream.

To serve, divide the sauce between four plates and top with the fillet of rudd
which has been carved into small pieces and left on a plate.  Spoon on the
crumble balls, spread the fillet with the sauce and serve with a dollop of sour cream.
Serve with potato wedges or crusty bread.
